ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of each UBO, general partner, limited partner holding more than 25%, manager and authorized signatory against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN/SSI Lists, the Luxembourg FIU's domestic sanctions/alert lists and national PEP registers. Matches are escalated to the designated AML/CFT officer and, where required, reported to the Cellule de Renseignements Financiers (CRF). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced IVD-manufacturing scope, including verification of source of funds, source of wealth, commercial counterparty reputation, and annual or event-driven rescreening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal, accessible via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are accepted in Latin script; French is the principal administrative language, with German and Luxembourgish also recognized. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into a Latin-script registered name, and any translated name must not be misleading. The SCSp name must comply with Luxembourg commercial-name law, must not conflict with existing registered names, and where applicable must carry the legal-form marker 'SCSp' or the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' in legal documents to avoid confusion.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: SA / SARL / Société Anonyme / Ltd / LLC
any term implying public authority, ministerial sponsorship, financial-services regulation, or misleading medical certification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/LBR rejects a requested name, the applicant should obtain the written reason for refusal and may, within three months of notification, file an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal through a licensed Luxembourg avocat. In respect of sensitive names requiring ministerial authorization, a renewed ministerial request may be submitted with corrected supporting documents. The applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative name; administrative appeal does not suspend the availability of a new filing. Fees paid for name clearance are not refunded upon rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as sole substance for this ISIC 3250 IVD-manufacturing scope. The SCSp must maintain a physical and verifiable registered office in Luxembourg; a pure virtual office is insufficient for RCS establishment authorization, VAT registration, AML/CFT supervision, and Ministry of Health medical-device manufacturing licensing. Service-provider registered-office addresses may support administrative form, but the licensed manufacturing operation requires actual operating premises and commercial substance in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Estimated 65% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation, driven by Ministry of Health medical-device manufacturing supervision, RCS commercial-substance controls, and AML/CFT on-site inspection of the licensed trust-company/registered-agent arrangement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Law on Commercial Companies of 10 August 1915), as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (Articles 101-108); Loi du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre de commerce et des sociétés; Règlement grand-ducal of 23 December 2016 on electronic filing and RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Trade and Companies Register, 13 rue Erasme, L-1468 Luxembourg; electronic filing via the e-RCS portal under the trusted third-party (TTP) accreditation mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution (Declaration of Constitution) filed electronically with the RCS, accompanied by the signed SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and followed by mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement. No escrow account or bank attestation de dépôt is required for the SCSp form, and full contribution need not be evidenced for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST MANAGEMENT RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER - RESOLUTION APPROVED ON [DATE].

The undersigned ultimate beneficial owner and general partner of [SCSp Name], a Luxembourg special limited partnership, hereby resolve: (1) to subscribe to the partnership interests set out in the partnership agreement and to confirm that no minimum paid-up capital is required under Luxembourg law; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address], Luxembourg; (3) to appoint [Name/Company] as manager of the SCSp with day-to-day administration powers and to authorize the manager, jointly and severally, to open bank accounts, file the declaration of constitution with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, and engage tax and legal counsel. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online search portal (www.lbr.lu / www.rcs.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative certificate search on the RCS electronic database for the proposed corporate name, verifying the absence of identical or confusingly similar names. Confirm that the name includes the mandatory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' and does not imply a legal form inconsistent with the partnership. Reserve the name on the e-RCS platform where the LBR offers an optional reservation.
required_dossiers: Proposed name list (primary and two alternates)
Identification documents of proposed partners
Certificate of trade mark search (optional but recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of identity, confusion, or misleading character, file written representations with the LBR registrar or select an alternative name. A definitive refusal may be appealed before the Luxembourg District Court within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or qualified corporate law firm; for an SCSp a notarial deed is required only where contributions in kind include immovable property or rights subject to publicity, otherwise a private written deed suffices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) in English or French, setting out the identity of the general partner and limited partners, contribution obligations, profit-sharing ratio, governance rules, registered office address, and duration. Since an SCSp has no legal personality, the agreement must express the contractual terms of the special limited partnership. Execute the deed by all partners and, where a notarial act is required, submit the signed draft plus partner identity documentation to the notary for authentication.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all partners
Proof of residence and address of each partner
Draft SCSp partnership agreement
Beneficial owner identification declarations under the Law of 13 January 2019
Information sheets (OCR) for RCS data input
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the legal form, governance clause, or contribution provisions, amend the partnership agreement by a unanimous partners' resolution and re-file. If a notarial act was required, the notary shall issue a rectification deed; any third-party reliance is cured prospectively upon RESA publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the declaration of constitution with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - e-RCS electronic filing portal; filing by a lawyer, notary, certified accountant, or other accredited TTP filer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the e-RCS 'déclaration de constitution' form and authenticate the filer's identity using the Trusted Third Party (TTP) training. Upload the executed partnership agreement and the statutory particulars: corporate name, registered office, object, general partner identity and signature powers, manager(s) acceptance, and expected value-added tax timetable. Pay the LBR filing fee and the registration duty. The registrar examines statutory compliance and may request clarifications before inscription.
required_dossiers: Declaration of constitution form (electronic signature)
Executed SCSp partnership agreement
Statement of acceptance of office by the general partner and by any appointed managers
Certified copies of identity of the general partner and managers
Proof of registered office address (lease or title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, respond to the query letter within 14 days by providing the corrected documents and amended declaration. A final refusal may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court within three months; in practice the LBR will accept a revised filing without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice in the RESA official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), published by the Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the legal notice for publication in the RESA. Review the draft extraction for accuracy of corporate name, legal form 'SCSp', registered office, partners' identity, and corporate object. The publication makes the constitution deed opposable to third parties and is a condition for the legal effect of the registration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extrait du RCS)
Authorization letter signed by the general partner for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains errors, file a formal rectification request with the RCS and pay the supplemental publication fee; the corrected notice operates prospectively from the date of rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, economic operator, and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers for the r.b.e. (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs and Registre économique); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, file VAT Form 1 with the AEDT within 15 days to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number and the r.b.e. economic operator number. The RCS data is shared with the AEDT, but explicit tax status elections must be made; for a transparent SCSp, ensure the pass-through classification is confirmed and no corporate income tax or net wealth tax applies in the absence of taxable substance. If the SCSp will employ staff, register with the CCSS and the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for occupational accident insurance.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Executed SCSp partnership agreement
VAT Form 1 (full name, address, activity code ISIC 3250)
Beneficial owner declarations for the RBE
CCSS registration form and manager identity (if employing staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or r.b.e. registration is delayed, follow up through the guichet 'cdf.lu' and request expedited treatment; if the SCSp is deemed to have a permanent establishment or taxable substance, appoint tax counsel and file a corrective declaration. Errors in the r.b.e. file can be corrected online within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institutions regulated by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), including BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, Spuerkeess, and private banks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full KYC/KYB file to the chosen bank under CSSF AML/CFT rules. Given the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML tier for IVD manufacturing and international payment rails (SWIFT letters of credit and TT wire), the bank will perform enhanced due diligence on all partners, beneficial owners, and sanctioned-country exposure. Provide source-of-funds evidence and a business plan. The bank will activate the account with e-banking and trade finance facilities.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (original or certified within 3 months)
SCSp partnership agreement
Lease contract for the registered office
Notarized/certified identity documents of all partners and beneficial owners
Bank reference and source-of-funds statements for capital contributions
Business plan and pro-forma financials for ISIC 3250 operations
Declaration of expected payment rails: SWIFT LC and TT wire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information under Article 3(2) of the CSSF regulation, provide the required documents within 15 days; if the account is declined, submit an enhanced due diligence pack to an alternative Luxembourg bank or appoint a professional trustee to facilitate the KYC process. There is no administrative appeal, so a parallel application to a second institution is the standard cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial establishment license and IVD manufacturing authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Guichet Unique pour le Commerce et l'Artisanat; Ministère de la Santé - Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments (DPM); Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the autorisation d'établissement application to the Guichet Unique of the Ministry of the Economy, demonstrating the manager's professional qualifications and absence of disqualifying criminal or bankruptcy records. For the IVD manufacturing activity, register the legal manufacturer in EUDAMED, appoint a Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC), and establish the technical documentation and quality management system compliant with ISO 13485. Class B and Class C devices require a notified body assessment; the Ministry of Health issues free-sale certificates for CE-marked IVDs destined for export.
required_dossiers: Autorisation d'établissement application form and fee
Diploma and criminal record (bulletin n°3) of the managing partner
Proof of professional indemnity insurance
Technical documentation and QMS (ISO 13485) summary
EUDAMED registration confirmation for the SCSp as legal manufacturer
Declaration of conformity for each IVD device class
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business license is refused, remedy by appealing to the Minister of the Economy within 40 days or by rectifying the professional qualification evidence. If the health authorization is queried, provide updated conformity assessment documentation or appoint an EU authorized representative; adverse notified body decisions are subject to the escalation procedure under Article 49 of Regulation (EU) 2017/746.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental classified establishment permit and civil defense clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency); communal building authority; Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the déclaration or demande de permis d'exploitation for the classified establishment under the Law of 30 July 2013 on establishments classified as dangerous, unhealthy, or noxious, specifying the ISO 3250 manufacturing processes (microfluidic cartridge molding, immunoassay reagent formulation, analyzer assembly). Submit the environmental permit application to the Administration de l'environnement with a noise assessment, wastewater plan, waste management plan, and safety report if required. Coordinate with ITM for occupational safety approval of the clean-room and wet-chemical areas, and obtain fire safety certification from CGDIS.
required_dossiers: Classified establishment registration/authorization form
Site plan and description of the production process
Wastewater discharge and air emission technical descriptions
Hazardous waste management contract with an approved collector (e.g., ANSV)
CGDIS fire safety certificate
ITM occupational safety clearance for equipment and chemical agents
Structural and electrical load certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental permit is silently refused or rejected, appeal to the administrative tribunal within one month; in the event of deficiencies in the dossier, a mise en complément letter requires amendment within 30 days. Fire safety and ITM observations must be corrected and re-inspections scheduled before operational start-up; continued non-compliance can result in a formal enforcement order with periodic penalty payments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Guichet Unique pour le Commerce et l'Artisanat for the business establishment license; Ministère de la Santé - Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments (DPM) for IVD manufacturer oversight; Administration de l'environnement for the classified environmental establishment permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (commercial and industrial establishment license) under the Law of 2 September 2011; permis d'exploitation (environmental operating permit) under the Law of 30 July 2013; Luxembourg manufacturer registration and EUDAMED notification as an in vitro diagnostic medical device manufacturer under Regulation (EU) 2017/746.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), acting under the authority of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 classified establishment (établissement classé) requiring a standard environmental operating permit (permis d'exploitation) with a simplified EIA registration; a full environmental impact assessment is triggered only if chemical wet-etching operations, volatile solvent consumption of 1 tonne per year or more, or clean-room energy demand exceed the Annex IV screening thresholds under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent limits: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 3 August 2009 and Directive 91/271/EEC; fugitive VOC emissions controlled under Directive 2010/75/EU with a solvent consumption reporting threshold of 2 tonnes per year; hazardous waste (etchants, immunoassay buffers, contaminated plastics) must be through an Administration de l'environnement approved collector and manifested to the Agency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection by the communal building authority and the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering work equipment verification, chemical agent risk assessment under REACH/CLP, hygiene of the clean-room environment, and employee medical surveillance schedule.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration; official portals: guichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, and aed.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register in the Luxembourg trade and companies register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal, obtain the national identification number (matricule), and then apply for VAT identification via MyGuichet.lu / AEDT. Non-established foreign suppliers without a fixed establishment register directly for Luxembourg VAT before making taxable supplies, subject to reverse-charge or OSS exceptions. The SCSp is registered by its general partner and is issued a Luxembourg national number and, where applicable, a VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box election. An SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent; it is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or net wealth tax, and its income is allocated to partners for taxation in their respective jurisdictions. Optional mechanisms include VAT grouping (assujetti unique), the simplified partnership taxation regime for direct tax, and disclosure/elections required under hybrid mismatch rules where the partnership is treated as transparent or opaque under foreign law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business exemption; non-established foreign taxable persons have no general registration threshold and must register from their first taxable supply unless reverse-charge, OSS, or IOSS applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a national continuous transaction control system. Electronic invoicing is permitted and PEPPOL B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for public procurement. Cross-border sellers of digital services may use the EU OSS/IOSS without local VAT registration; no real-time API clearance is currently enforced.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods supplied by the Luxembourg IVD manufacturer and physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier retains satisfactory evidence of export. Qualifying services include directly connected transport, handling, and offshore processing services provided to non-EU customers. The customer must be a taxable person located in a third country where the transfer of ownership or effective use occurs outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated EU customs export declaration (SAD / Export Accompanying Document)
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or CMR consignment note signed by the carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer proof evidencing receipt of payment from the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities apply risk-based export verification and may require complete documentation at audit. If zero-rating is not objectively substantiated, the supply is recharacterized as taxable in Luxembourg at 17% VAT, with late-payment interest accruing and administrative fines. Where fraudulent documentary claims are established, criminal prosecution may follow, allowing retrospective clawback of tax, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as the national central bank of Luxembourg within the Eurosystem under the monetary policy and foreign-reserve authority of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions rests with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro-area regime: full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account operations with no exchange-control approval requirement; Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital. The Luxembourg SCSp may freely open multi-currency accounts, retain USD/GBP/CHF/CNY proceeds, remit dividends and redeem partnership interests without BCL permission. The only operational constraint is the BCL Balance of Payments (BoP) statistical declaration duty under ECB Regulation (EU) No 1841/2018: every cross-border transaction at or above EUR 12,500 (or equivalent) must be reported to BCL by the client through the resident credit institution. Distributions from a fiscally transparent SCSp are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, but confirmatory legal certainty should be obtained via an advance tax ruling (tax clearance) from the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory conversion, no repatriation window, and no surrender obligation on export receivables. The IVD manufacturer may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at any CSSF-licensed institution, use them directly for offshore trade settlements, FX hedging, or treasury allocations, without central bank approval. The sole residual duty is statistical: each cross-border transaction equal to or above EUR 12,500 must be reported to BCL via the banking counterparty; EU and UN sanctions, dual-use and medical-device export controls apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Settlement Account (EUR/USD/CNH) with dedicated trade-finance and LC sub-limits
Operational Account plus Capital Escrow Account (EUR/USD) with SWIFT MT103 and MT700 documentary-credit capabilities
Operational and Commercial Cash Account for SCSp with optional escrow annex
Operational Transactional Account (multi-currency, corporate e-banking, payment factory)
Partnership Escrow and Wealth-Management Cash Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Spuerkeess (Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational treasury and global supplier disbursements; Low for statutory capital escrow. Luxembourg recognises Payment Institutions and E-Money Institutions under PSD2 (Law of 28 July 2020, amended, CSSF Regulation 12-02), including CSSF-licensed EMIs such as MultiPass (Luxembourg) and passported players such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, and Wise Platform; these EMIs can deliver virtual IBANs in EUR/GBP/USD, SWIFT MT103 equivalent transfers, and competitive mid-market FX. Legal constraints: (i) e-money balances are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (Fonds de garantie des dépôts) and must be safeguarded in segregated accounts at a credit institution; (ii) EMIs do not hold a banking licence under the Law of 5 April 1993 and therefore cannot operate a true escrow or hold client money in a protected capital-escrow structure; (iii) full UBO/KYC documentation of the SCSp still applies. Recommended architecture: keep capital and investor funds with a tier-1 bank and use the EMI as a settlement overlay for fast micro-supplier payments, corporate card programmes, and emerging-market currency routing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law (Law of 29 March 2023 on AML/CFT, repealing the 2004 framework) and CSSF Regulation 12-02 permit non-face-to-face onboarding with qualified video identification, but most commercial banks impose a mandatory physical interview for (i) the legal representative of the general partner, (ii) all limited partners holding 25% or more of the capital, and (iii) the ultimate signatories of the payment mandate. For a SCSp with non-EU limited partners, the bank normally requires the general partner's representative to appear in person at the bank's premises in Luxembourg, or before a Luxembourg notary with apostilled powers of attorney; remote opening is accepted only with notarised/apostilled constitutional documents, a video-verified UBO kit, and, in practice, a letter of comfort from the SCSp's legal counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp opacity: limited partners are not listed in the RCS extract; the bank cannot establish the ultimate ownership chain of the IVD manufacturing entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) fully executed Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) with capital-commitment schedule; (ii) RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) certificate of registration dated less than 30 days; (iii) UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract dated less than 3 months; (iv) signed beneficial-ownership declaration on CSSF Form D; (v) certified organisational chart of the general partner; (vi) passport copies of all limited partners and ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparency ambiguity: the bank's tax desk cannot determine withholding-tax classification of the distribution waterfall of the SCSp; account onboarding is suspended.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Luxembourg legal opinion confirming SCSp fiscal transparency; (ii) optional advance tax ruling from the ACD confirming pass-through status; (iii) certificate of non-assessment to Luxembourg corporate income tax for the SCSp; (iv) corporate tax-residence certificate of the general partner; (v) Luxembourg VAT (TVA) registration certificate evidencing the SCSp as a taxable person for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU investor money arriving in multiple tranches deliberately below EUR 12,500 to avoid BCL statistical reporting; source-of-funds doubts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) twelve months of original bank statements for each investing entity; (ii) notarised source-of-wealth questionnaire; (iii) audited or certified financial statements of corporate investors; (iv) executed subscription agreements cross-referencing the LPA capital accounts; (v) signed declaration that no third-party back-to-back funding is used; (vi) written AML sign-off by the receiving bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EWRA (Enhanced With Respect to Risk Assessment) flag on point-of-care IVD trade flows from emerging-market distributors; dual-use and medical-device export-control screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) EU CE-mark certificates under IVDR (EU) 2017/746 for analyzers and microfluidic cartridges; (ii) Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Laboratoire national de santé) or authorised-notified-body registration; (iii) signed distribution agreements and end-user undertakings; (iv) export licences or no-licence determinations; (v) ISO 13485 certificate for the manufacturing process; (vi) commercial invoices, bills of lading, air waybills, and certificates of origin for each flagged shipment; (vii) sanctions-screening output and consolidated screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-control concern: the sole general partner is a single-director company; risk of unauthorised disbursements of escrowed capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) certified extract from the Luxembourg business register on the general partner's directors; (ii) board resolution approving the signing mandate, the 4-eyes rule, and the list of authorised signatories; (iii) valid e-passports of all signatories; (iv) notarised and apostilled power of attorney for non-resident signatories; (v) bank confirmation of dual-swipe authentication and call-back verification procedure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All investor subscriptions above EUR 12,500 must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 (SEPA pacs.008 for euro contributions) with Field 70 (Remittance Information) containing 'SCSP [name] - CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - LPA CLAUSE [X]', the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference), the remitter name exactly matching the UBO register, and the applicable ECB BoP purpose code (e.g., 'DK' for direct-investment equity capital or 'V' for participation capital) as instructed by the receiving bank. The receiving bank verifies the remitter against the RBE/UBO files, reconciles the amount against the capital-commitment schedule of the LPA, confirms the absence of third-party interposition, and reports the transaction to BCL under its BoP reporting obligation. For amounts below EUR 12,500, the bank must still report aggregated flows. All inbound capital should be received only at the Luxembourg relationship bank's branch and never via an unverified intermediary account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) EEA suppliers of microfluidic raw materials and immunoassay reagents: SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 pain.001/pacs.008 with dual-authorisation and same-day settlement; (ii) Asia/US component procurement: SWIFT MT103 against commercial invoices, packing lists and air waybills, with UETR tracking for open-account; for capital equipment, an irrevocable documentary credit issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank via SWIFT MT700 (UCP 600), advised by MT710, reimbursed by MT202, with standby LC (MT760) used as security for toll-manufacturing contracts; (iii) sales-side collection from hospitals and distributors: sight letters of credit (MT700/MT754) on first-class banks, SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers with 30-90 day terms, and SWIFT gpi for real-time fund tracking; (iv) treasury concentration: EUR concentration at BIL or BGL BNP Paribas, USD concentration via the bank's US correspondent, and cross-currency sweeps through the relationship bank's FX desk to achieve netting; SWIFT MT103 remains the primary rail for all non-SEPA cross-border disbursements in the target payment rails of Swift_LC and TT_Wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (FXA) with tenors from 1 to 24 months for USD-denominated IVD export receivables
FX swap (spot-start and tom-next) to bridge USD/GBP/CHF receipts into EUR operating liquidity
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD, fixed-for-floating) for project-finance tranches and large capex commitments
Vanilla EUR/USD options and zero-cost collars (risk reversal) for downside protection on bundled analyzer-and-cartridge contracts
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on emerging-market currencies (INR, CNY, BRL, SAR) referenced to EUR-equivalent exposure, permitted when the underlying invoice currency is non-convertible or restricted
FX swap-based intraday liquidity sweeps and notional pooling overlays within the Luxembourg banking group

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels) with RESA publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (calendar-year SCSp: partner approval within 6 months and filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered fine of EUR 25–5,000 per missing document under Art. 16 of the law of 19 December 2002; failure to file for 3 consecutive years enables the Public Prosecutor to petition judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually, within 1 month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any transfer of SCSp partnership interests must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500–37,500 and/or 1 month–1 year imprisonment for responsible managers under Art. 35 of the amended law of 13 January 2019; outstanding confirmation blocks issuance of certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) for CE-marked Class C/D IVD devices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Notified Body under Regulation (EU) 2017/746, Art. 81; retained for Luxembourg Ministry of Health inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually on the anniversary of the CE certificate issue date; additional updates upon significant post-market vigilance events
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or withdrawal of the CE certificate, prohibiting EU market placement of the automated point-of-care IVD; administrative fines and corrective-action orders under the Luxembourg medical devices law of 8 January 2022.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé when the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, average workforce over 50 employees (Art. 69, law of 19 December 2002).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalisé) under the law of 19 December 2002; IFRS optional for non-listed entities and mandatory for consolidated financial statements; all statutory accounts denominated in EUR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp general partner (commandité) must annually confirm the RBE record within 1 month of the registration anniversary; every transfer of limited-partnership interests must be reported within 30 days and entered in the partnership register to be opposable to third parties; the annual confirmation is a condition for obtaining a certificate of good standing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Minutes and Resolutions (Registre des procès-verbaux et décisions)
Register of Partnership-Interest Transfers (Registre des cessions de parts)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900–2,500 per year for licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000–45,000 per year for statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé; plus USD 3,500–16,000 per year for IVDR notified-body surveillance and PSUR review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for a Luxembourg City taxable corporate (17% CIT + 1.19% unemployment solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to corporate income tax at entity level
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp pass-through taxation: profits are taxed directly in the hands of partners; non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment are generally exempt from Luxembourg tax. Where a taxable corporate exists: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% holding or EUR 1.2m acquisition cost, 12-month holding period), 80% IP Box exemption for qualifying IVD patents and copyrighted software, 0% withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties, and no net wealth tax for fully non-resident transparent structures without a Luxembourg PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (CIT declaration for companies) / partnership declaration Form 520 for transparent SCSp; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu portal and the eCDF platform of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar year or approved fiscal year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March of the year following the taxable year for calendar-year filers; automatic extension to 31 December of the following year for electronically filed returns; non-calendar fiscal years: due within 3 months of year-end, extendable by 9 months on e-filing; further extension only upon reasoned request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, fiscal address, status of winding-up, and permanent establishment indicators
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the SCSp name and RCS number; appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative if no local director. Declare whether any partner is non-resident and confirm the absence of a Luxembourg PE for all non-resident partners

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form classification and tax treatment election (transparent partnership versus taxable company)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'SCSp – Société en Commandite Spéciale' under the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013. Confirm that the SCSp is fiscally transparent and attach the partnership agreement and partner register

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-by-partner allocation of income, deductions, and tax credits; includes the partnership allocation schedule annexed to the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner provide full legal name, country of residence, tax identification number, and profit-sharing ratio. Non-resident partners report only Luxembourg-source items (e.g., Luxembourg PE profit, Luxembourg real estate income) in their own jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims under Article 166 LIR for exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach evidence of 10% minimum shareholding (or EUR 1.2m acquisition cost), 12-month holding commitment, and compliance with the subject-to-tax condition for the subsidiary. Non-resident partners must map the claim to the relevant DTA article

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net qualifying IP income and the 80% exemption under Article 50ter LIR for patents, copyrighted software, and other qualifying intangibles
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IVD microfluidic cartridge and immunoassay analyzer IP must be developed or improved in Luxembourg; attach the nexus ratio calculation and R&D expenditure tracking. Non-resident partners cannot benefit from the IP Box absent a Luxembourg PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 / Foreign tax credits and DTA relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income and unilateral/treaty credits under Article 134bis LIR and applicable tax treaties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete for each non-resident partner any foreign withholding tax on IVD royalties or dividends; attach tax residence certificates and source-country tax vouchers to substantiate credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax (Art. 155 LIR); default interest of 0.9% per month on arrears (Art. 153 LIR); estimated assessment on non-filing; intentional non-filing constitutes tax fraud punishable by a fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Art. 396-399 General Tax Law); continued default after court order may trigger commercial court dissolution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard statutory rate; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and 0% under the domestic participation exemption where the corporate partner holds at least 10% (or EUR 1.2m) for 12 months; for a transparent SCSp, distributions of profits to partners are not subject to dividend withholding tax at the partnership level because the profits retain their character and source in the partners' hands
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (i) obtain a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (ACD Form 261-RCD) for the SCSp or corporate partner and an equivalent residence certificate from the foreign partner's tax authority confirming treaty residence; (ii) submit both certificates to the Luxembourg paying entity before the distribution or payment date; (iii) file the standardised exemption/refund application with the ACD within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years); (iv) document the beneficial owner status and economic substance; Luxembourg applies the principal purpose test and may deny relief where the SCSp is used as a conduit without real commercial activity
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic withholding tax on outbound IP royalties. Interest: 0% domestic withholding tax on outbound debt interest, except for certain savings income, profit-participating loans, and back-to-back/hybrid arrangements. Where no domestic WHT applies, treaty reduction is unnecessary but treaty entitlement still requires substantive DTA residence

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory and must be filed annually with the tax return where the group's consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50 million; Master File is required where the group's consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 750 million; Country-by-Country Report applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million (Law of 28 December 2018 and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 6 December 2019). An SCSp with IVD manufacturing and intercompany supply must also maintain contemporaneous benchmarking documentation below the thresholds if it has related-party transactions
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) – preferred for commodities and standard IVD components
Resale Price Method – suitable for distribution of manufactured microfluidic cartridges
Cost Plus Method – appropriate for contract manufacturing of immunoassay analyzers
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) – accepted as a fallback using PLI (net margin) of tested party
Profit Split Method – required where both parties make unique intangibles contributions or risks are integrated
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, Articles 6 and 6bis of the Tax Adaptation Law (GAAR), ATAD rules, and the OECD principal purpose test demand genuine economic substance: real employees, physical premises in Luxembourg, local decision-making, and risk management commensurate with the IVD manufacturing functions. The SCSp must demonstrate commercial rationale for its existence; passive cash-box or conduit arrangements without substance risk reclassification, denial of treaty benefits, and full 24.94% re-taxation with penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate submission of false declarations, concealment of IVD device sales revenue, fictitious invoicing, falsified partner allocations, or artificial shifting of profit to tax haven entities through the SCSp
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud: fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Art. 396-399 General Tax Law); 10% omission surcharge plus 0.9% monthly default interest; civil re-assessment at the full 24.94% combined rate with compound penalties for gross negligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers (gérants), and authorised signatories face joint and several civil liability for misstated returns; personal assets may be seized; travel bans and preventive detention may be ordered where departure would jeopardise collection; criminal conviction leads to disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp interposed with negligible substance solely to obtain treaty benefits on IVD royalties, dividends, or capital gains; round-tripping structures, artificial conduit arrangements, or back-to-back licensing without real commercial justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification under Article 6 Tax Adaptation Law and denial of treaty benefits; retroactive taxation at 24.94% aggregate rate; penalty interest of 0.9% monthly; application of EU ATAD III (Unshell) minimum substance indicators and mandatory automatic exchange of information with partner-state tax authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and corporate directors may be held personally liable for the full tax re-assessment where they knowingly implemented the abusive arrangement; directors face fines and up to 5 years' imprisonment for complicity in fiscal fraud; ATAD III disclosures expose directors to cross-border reputational and regulatory action

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file the Local File when group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; absence of a contemporaneous benchmarking study for intercompany IVD cartridge supply, royalty payments, or risk allocation; non-arm's-length profit margins on Luxembourg functions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 per missing or materially deficient document; primary tax adjustment of the Luxembourg taxable base; additional 10% 'considerable under-declaration' surcharge; default interest at 0.9% per month on the corrected tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany agreements or approve transfer pricing without supporting documentation risk personal civil liability for the resulting tax shortfall; courts may issue travel bans where the director's exit could impede collection; criminal sanctions for knowingly preparing false TP documentation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform due diligence (KYC/KYB) on non-resident limited partners; omission to file suspicious transaction reports (STR) with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) for irregular Swift LC or TT wire payments; dealing with sanctioned or embargoed jurisdictions in IVD equipment sales; acceptance of unexplained third-party payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million under the Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended); criminal money-laundering penalties: imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000 for simple laundering, and up to 10 years for aggravated or organised laundering; freezing of bank accounts and corporate assets; professional disqualification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, AML compliance officers, and the RCS-designated administrator (where applicable) are personally liable for failed supervision; travel bans and passport seizure are available preventive coercive measures; statutory managers may be disqualified from practising for up to 10 years and imprisoned; the corporate veil is pierced for gross negligence in AML control

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain proper accounting records for the SCSp, failure to file annual accounts with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) where required, or refusal to produce books upon ACD inspection; falsification of the partner register or capital accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 plus daily penalties for continued default; compulsory winding-up proceedings before the commercial court; disqualification of the responsible manager; interest and surcharges on any resulting tax adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable for damages caused to third parties and creditors resulting from the absence of reliable financial statements; personal conviction for filing false accounts; travel bans where non-filing masks assets; permanent prohibition from holding managerial office in Luxembourg entities
